clue.text: Saturated but deliberately by lumbermen?

definitions.meaning: lumbermen float felled trees down rivers on purpose, so timber is logged by water deliberately

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as WATER-LOGGED: what the lumbermen do on purpose is send their logs by water.
explanation.definitionFit: Something soaked through until it can hold no more liquid is saturated; the second sense is timber floated downstream.

clue.text: Shuffle the deck in cunning indeed in sinful fashion

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged card word inside the word for cunning

parts.note: wily means cunning, and indeed adds emphasis

indicators.note: shuffling the deck rearranges its order, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A card sharp shuffles the pack craftily and wickedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shuffle' mixes DECK into CKED, which goes 'in' WILY. 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing wrong in an evil way, wicked behaviour.

clue.text: Like Miranda's love-story ?

parts.note: Miranda is the heroine of Shakespeare's The Tempest, so her romance is stormy in a punning sense

explanation.definitionFit: Stormy and turbulent, as the title of her play suggests.

clue.text: Bernardo provided a welcome one to Francisco

definitions.text: Bernardo provided a welcome one to Francisco

parts.words: Bernardo provided a welcome one to Francisco
parts.note: at the start of Hamlet the sentry Bernardo takes over the watch from Francisco, who says 'For this ... much thanks'

explanation.definitionFit: Taking over a guard's watch frees him from duty, which is the comfort Francisco thanks him for.

clue.text: Submits to Turkish V.I.P. in largest size

indicators.note: in places the Turkish dignitary inside the size abbreviation

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, the biggest clothing size
a bey was a Turkish governor or nobleman

explanation.surface: Someone yields to an important Turk in the biggest clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize, a British clothing label for the largest size) holds BEY.
explanation.definitionFit: To comply with an order or authority is to give way to it.

clue.text: Tribal Rialto wear ?

parts.note: Shylock in The Merchant of Venice complains of being spat upon on the Rialto in his 'Jewish ...', the badge of all his tribe

explanation.definitionFit: A loose long cloak of coarse cloth, the garment Shylock wore in Venice.

clue.text: The doctor has only half Eliza's love

indicators.note: keeping only half of the two round letters (two loves, tennis zeros) in Eliza's surname leaves just one

parts.note: Eliza Doolittle is the flower girl in Shaw's Pygmalion and My Fair Lady

explanation.surface: A physician wins only half of a flower girl's affection.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliza's surname has two Os, each a tennis 'love'; 'has only half' her love keeps one of them, giving the doctor of Hugh Lofting's children's books, who talks to animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor Dolittle is the animal-talking physician in Hugh Lofting's stories.

clue.text: Welcome back, she says

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for welcome from right to left

parts.note: ave is the Latin greeting meaning hail or welcome

explanation.surface: A woman calls out a greeting from behind the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns AVE, the Latin hail, into EVA; 'says' is a link and 'she' the definition, a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Eva is a female first name, so it stands for any woman, a she.

clue.text: Priestly contributor to the literary supplement

definitions.note: an adjective standing for the noun: the Old Testament priest at Shiloh who raised Samuel

indicators.note: the words supply a few of their own letters, contributing them to the answer

explanation.surface: A clergyman writes for a literary review.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'thE LIterary'; 'supplement' finishes the surface. The definition is loose, an adjective for a priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Eli was the high priest at Shiloh in the Book of Samuel.

clue.text: Mountain marksman ?

definitions.meaning: a holy peak in northern Greece, home to monasteries
one of Dumas's Three Musketeers, a musket being a gun

explanation.definitionFit: Mount Athos is the Greek monastic peninsula's peak; Athos is also a musketeer, a man with a gun.

clue.text: It gives one the hump to have arrived at the half century

parts.note: came means arrived
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, half of a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone sulks at reaching the age of fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives one the hump' means makes someone sulky in British slang, but here it is literal: this animal carries a hump. 'to have' and 'at the' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The dromedary carries a fatty lump on its back, so it literally bears the hump.

clue.text: Make far from plain

parts.note: reads like making something obscure or hard to understand, but means making something ornate rather than plain

explanation.definitionFit: To decorate with ornaments is to make a thing fancy instead of unadorned.

clue.text: French learners include a Pole in their teams

indicators.note: include tells us the French pupils take the pole letter within them

parts.note: eleves is the French word for pupils
N stands for the north pole

explanation.surface: French schoolchildren admit a Polish boy into their sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a Pole' looks like a Polish person but is N, the north pole, which goes inside ELEVES. 'in their' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket and football sides have eleven players each, so such sides are called elevens.

clue.text: Reprimands on the lower deck

definitions.meaning: ordinary sailors below officer rank in the navy, who live on the lower deck

explanation.definitionFit: A rating is a scolding; it is also a naval seaman without a commission, a member of the lower deck.

clue.text: Old man who held a tanner concealed?

indicators.note: the words held a tanner are disguised, their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An old man who kept a sixpence hidden away.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner is old British slang for a sixpence coin. 'concealed' rearranges HELD A TANNER; 'who' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Neanderthal man is an extinct early human, prehistoric man.

clue.text: " As bright Apollo's -- ,strung with his hair " (L.L. Lost)

definitions.text: " As bright Apollo's -- ,strung with his hair " (L.L. Lost)

parts.words: " As bright Apollo's -- ,strung with his hair " (L.L. Lost)
parts.note: a line from Shakespeare's Love's Labour's Lost, where Berowne says love is as sweet and musical as the stringed instrument of the god Apollo

explanation.definitionFit: Apollo, god of music, is pictured playing a stringed instrument of the guitar family, which Berowne imagines strung with his hair.

clue.text: Fairy, spotless-and at the best age

parts.note: a peri is a fairy in Persian myth
clean means spotless

explanation.surface: A fairy is immaculate and in her prime.
explanation.walkthrough: The age of Pericles was the golden age of ancient Athens, hence 'the best age'. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to Pericles, whose rule marked the high point of Athenian culture, a golden era.

clue.text: One eats this steak of course out of bed

indicators.note: the course word lies outside the bed word, wrapping it

parts.note: an entree is a course of a meal
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A diner eats steak as a course while out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' means outside: the course wraps round the bed. 'One eats this' is part of the definition, since the steak is a thing eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrecote is a boneless cut from between the ribs, eaten as a beef dish.

clue.text: There's a case for walking

parts.note: reads as an argument in favour of going on foot, but a medical case is a patient, and one able to walk is described this way

explanation.definitionFit: A patient able to move on foot rather than on a stretcher is called a walking case.

clue.text: Investment that might call for a runner ?

definitions.text: Investment that might call for a runner ?

parts.words: Investment that might call for a runner ?
parts.note: investment is the military sense of besieging a place, and a ship slipping through a naval siege is a runner

explanation.definitionFit: A siege that cuts off supplies is evaded by a blockade runner.

clue.text: Like Lovelace's linnets

parts.note: Richard Lovelace's poem To Althea, from Prison begins a stanza 'When, like ... linnets, I', comparing himself in jail to caged songbirds

explanation.definitionFit: The poet's caged birds are shut up in confinement, as a prisoner is consigned to jail.

clue.text: I perform at 50 and still have my admirers !

definitions.note: the speaker is one who is adored by fans; a verb phrase standing for the noun

parts.note: do means perform
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An ageing performer boasts of still having fans at fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue speaks as the person adored: someone still admired is a figure of worship. 'at' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop star or film star worshipped by fans is one who has admirers.

clue.text: Easily persuaded to plan it differently

indicators.note: differently says the letters of plan it are arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone is quick to agree to rework a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' rearranges PLAN IT; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pliant person is flexible and readily influenced.

clue.text: " My right there is none to -" (Cowper )

definitions.text: " My right there is none to -" (Cowper )

parts.words: " My right there is none to -" (Cowper )
parts.note: from Cowper's verses on Alexander Selkirk: 'I am monarch of all I survey, My right there is none to ...', meaning no one can challenge it

explanation.definitionFit: To challenge or contest a claim is what nobody can do to the castaway's right.

clue.text: Eve is decidedly brunette

parts.note: reads as a remark about a woman's hair colour, but eve also means evening, which is dark-toned

explanation.definitionFit: Dark-complexioned, as twilight is dim.

clue.text: Sir Lancelot's was blazon'd

parts.note: Tennyson's Lady of Shalott: 'From the blazon'd ... slung A mighty silver bugle hung'

explanation.definitionFit: A shoulder belt worn across the body to carry a sword or bugle, decorated with heraldry on Lancelot.

clue.text: Two and one for the General

parts.note: both means the two
a means one

explanation.surface: Two soldiers and one more for the commander.
explanation.walkthrough: Louis Botha was a Boer general and the first Prime Minister of South Africa. 'and' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Botha led Boer forces in the South African War as a commander.

clue.text: Mrs. Behn minds a harp

indicators.note: minds, in the sense of tends or sees to, signals that the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: The playwright looks after a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minds' rearranges A HARP. Aphra Behn was a seventeenth-century English playwright and novelist.

clue.text: Longing for some happy ending

indicators.note: some of tells us the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Wishing for a story that finishes well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes a run of letters across 'happY ENding'; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A yen is a strong desire or craving.

clue.text: Inspiration of a Gallic festival

parts.note: the French national day on 14 July commemorates the storming of the Paris prison fortress in 1789
